prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your exact needs (home size, ductwork condition, budget, preferred equipment brands, timeline). I can find highly rated local companies for you if you tell me your Atlanta zip code. Meanwhile, here’s a practical way to choose and what to expect.

Quick questions so I can help:
- Is this for a house or a business?
- Zip code or neighborhood in Atlanta?
- Preferred equipment (brand or heat pump vs straight AC)?
- Rough budget or timeline?

How to pick the right company (check these)
- Proper credentials: EPA 608 certification (for refrigerants), local/ county licensing if required, liability insurance.
- Experience & certifications: NATE-certified technicians, manufacturer factory-authorized dealer for the brand you want.
- Written Manual J load calculation (right size the system) and Manual D if ductwork changes are needed.
- Clear written estimate: equipment model & SEER, labor, permit fees, scope of work, replacement of components (thermostat, disconnect, pads), disposal of old unit.
- Warranties: equipment warranty (manufacturer) and labor/installation warranty (contractor). Ask about extended labor warranties.
- References & reviews: Google, Angi (formerly Angie’s List), BBB, and recent customer reviews.
- Permits & inspections: contractor should obtain permits and schedule required inspections.
- Rebates & incentives: check Georgia Power and federal/state incentives (especially for high-efficiency systems or heat pumps).

Sample questions to ask each contractor
- Are your techs NATE certified? Can you provide proof of insurance and licensing?
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and include it with the quote?
- Which exact model (make/model number) are you proposing and why?
- What is the SEER rating and estimated seasonal energy cost?
- What parts of the system are covered by manufacturer and what by you (labor)?
- Who does the warranty service if there’s a problem after install?
- Do you handle permits and sweep/disconnect/recycle old unit?
- Can you give references for recent Atlanta AC replacements?

Expected ballpark cost (Atlanta metro, residential central AC replacement)
- Typical range: about $4,000–$12,000+ depending on tonnage, SEER, ductwork needed, and brand. Small simple replacements can be toward the low end; high-efficiency or larger homes with duct repairs can be much higher.
- Get 3 written quotes to compare apples-to-apples (same equipment and scope).

Where to find contractors
- Local review sites: Google Maps, Yelp, Angi, BBB.
- Manufacturer locator tools: Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Goodman, etc., to find factory-authorized dealers in Atlanta.
- Utility rebate pages (Georgia Power) and ENERGY STAR or IRS/DOE pages for federal incentives.

If you want, give me your zip code and whether you prefer specific brands or a heat pump, and I’ll pull 3–5 well-reviewed Atlanta-area contractors with recent ratings and what each one is known for.
